what: what a precompiled script image saves on a WHOLE page load, not on one stage
machine: devbox, AMD EPYC 9V45, 8 cores, clang 24, Release
tool: ctcompile/tools/ctpageload, run from ctbrowser/examples/pages so the page's <script src> resolves
page: p5-basic.html - three classic scripts: an inline flag, the p5 bundle, and the sketch
findings: MORE THAN HALF OF THIS PAGE'S LOAD WAS COMPILING ITS JAVASCRIPT. 72.59 ms becomes 34.25 ms, and what remains is HTML parsing, CSS, style, layout and the image load itself - the work Principle 6 says stays at run time.

THE MEASUREMENT PROVES THE PATH WAS TAKEN rather than assuming it: the tool exits non-zero unless browser::scripts_compiled_from_source() is 0 after the image run. It reported 'the image was REFUSED' twice during development - once because the tool guessed the script concatenation wrong, once because the page's <script src> did not resolve from the working directory - and both times the saving it printed would otherwise have been read as a finding.

A TOOL MUST NOT REPRODUCE THE BROWSER'S CONCATENATION. p5-basic.html has THREE classic scripts, not the one-bundle-plus-sketch shape the first version assumed; a packager that guesses builds an image whose hash never matches, which presents as 'no saving' rather than as a bug. browser::script_source() exists for this and is the API a packager uses.
THE IMAGE IS 1.6x THE SOURCE for this page and the page still loads twice as fast. Size is not the figure of merit; the parse is.
